headline_finding: THE GAP LIST IS DECAYING IN REAL TIME, AND BLSH IS THE ONLY NAME NOT PARTICIPATING. Three successive pulls this run: 10 rows >=5% at 10:09 ET, then 6 rows at 10:13 ET, with every single down-gap narrowing over those four minutes — CRWV -5.21 -> -4.27, LUNR -5.31 -> -4.15, QBTS -5.02 -> -4.08, ONDS -6.97 -> -5.72, NBIS -6.26 -> -5.57, BE -5.92 -> -5.10, and APT's up-gap fading +5.18 -> +3.72. The three names that led the 09:09 list have fallen out of the scan entirely (BMNR -7.62 -> -4.49, AMKR -5.23 -> -4.13, BW -5.26 -> -3.40). SPY and QQQ were flat across the same window (745.06 vs 744.95; 665.74 vs 665.35), so this is single-name mean reversion off the open, not an index rally. The exception is BLSH, pinned at exactly -6.18% ($21.10, unchanged tick for tick) while its entire cohort bounced — it finished the run as the WIDEST gap on the board after starting 4th. Relative weakness that refuses a cohort-wide bid, two sessions ahead of a pre-market print with a double-digit implied move and deteriorating operating metrics, is a warning, not a setup.

headlines: Ondas Q3 2026: revenue $167.5M (+100% q/q), backlog $835M, FY26 target raised to >=$550M, >$165M of new orders since the last update (Reddit r/ONDS, 2026-11-13)

gappers.catalyst_detail: Ondas reported Q3 2026 revenue of $167.5M, roughly double the prior quarter, with an $835M backlog, a raised FY26 revenue target of at least $550M, and more than $165M of new orders booked since its last update. The counter-drone and ISR franchise is real and growing — Rotron Aero, American Robotics' Optimus, the ONBERG joint venture in Germany, 2026 FIFA World Cup counter-drone work, a >$50M border demining tender. None of that changed today. What changed is the tape: ONDS carries a ~2.9 beta and short interest reported above 40% of float, so it moves roughly 3x the index in either direction.
gappers.why: High-beta microcap with a crowded long and a large short base, de-rating on index beta rather than news. With QQQ -2.1% and no bid under the AI complex at the open, recent earnings buyers became the marginal sellers — then the move began reversing as soon as that flow exhausted.
gappers.impact: Reads as a one-day beta spike, not a fundamental break, and the intraday evidence supports that: the gap narrowed from -6.97% to -5.72% in four minutes with no news. The prior session's 8.65M shares is heavy, but the volume that matters is today's and it is not yet measurable. Sector read-through is uniform — NBIS, CRWV, BE, QBTS and LUNR all gapped 5-7% on the same list and all bounced together, confirming a factor move rather than an ONDS problem.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: The order-book story is structural, but today's move is pure factor beta into a binary (NVDA Tuesday PM) and is already mean-reverting — there is no durable multi-day thesis in a gap that half-closes before the scan finishes.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Displaces nothing: 0 open positions, 0/3 weekly trades used, $100,000 cash. The binding constraint is R:R, not capacity. ATR(14) is $0.43 = 9.0% of price, so the mandated 10% trailing stop sits at just 1.11 ATR — inside normal daily noise — and clearing 2:1 needs +20% (2.21 ATR) from a stop that cannot hold. It also fails the long-bias filter (below both 20- and 200-SMA, per the 07:09/08:08 ET runs), and buying a down-gap with no symbol-specific catalyst is forbidden outright. No entry.

gappers.catalyst_detail: Amprius posted record Q3 2026 revenue of $39.1M, up 83% from $21.4M a year earlier, with management citing sustained demand for its energy-dense silicon-anode lithium-ion cells; the company remains loss-making at the net line. The print landed 2026-11-11 and the stock rose on it. Today's gap carries no new company news. AMPX trades as a 'physical AI' derivative — drones, eVTOL, defense payloads — so it de-rates on the same factor as the compute names despite having no AI-capex exposure of its own.
gappers.why: A pre-profitability, long-duration growth story whose valuation is almost entirely terminal value. When the AI/duration factor sells off, the discount rate on that terminal value rises and the equity drops hard regardless of the quarter just reported.
gappers.impact: The prior session's 765k shares is unremarkable for AMPX, and the gap narrowed from -6.68% to -5.49% in four minutes — both point to thin, headline-less beta rather than a repricing, which makes this the more mean-reversion-prone end of the list. Read-through is sector-wide (ONDS, LUNR on the same board), so there is no idiosyncratic edge to isolate. Worth noting it entered the scan as the cohort rotated: crypto-treasury and semi names (BMNR, AMKR, BW) stabilized out of the list while drone/battery/space/quantum names rotated in.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: Thin-volume, catalyst-free beta drawdown in a loss-making name; nothing structural happened today, and the sector-rotation table does not favor speculative battery/physical-AI exposure while the factor is in drawdown.

headlines: Nebius Q3 2026: revenue $980.8M, +571% y/y, adjusted EBITDA positive at $465.8M, capex $7.3B in the quarter (NFC Market Live, 2026-11-12)
Nebius Q3 2026 earnings review: investors contrast the call unfavorably with CoreWeave's handling of the same concerns (Reddit r/NBIS_Stock, 2026-11-13)
gappers.catalyst_detail: This is the one name on the list where the de-rate is NOT catalyst-free, and the 09:09 ET run established why: Q3 revenue of $980.8M (+571% y/y) and positive adjusted EBITDA of $465.8M beat, but Nebius cut the top end of FY26 guidance, flagged capacity delays, and guided capex toward roughly $45B — then Baird cut its price target from $340 to $200 and BofA to $265. The market is no longer paying for AI-infrastructure revenue growth funded at that scale; it is discounting the financing risk. Huang's resignation removed the most credible voice underwriting the AI-capex cycle, and Musk's 'neocloud collapse' warning has been circulating against the same group.
gappers.why: A levered, capex-funded buildout re-rates on cost of capital, not on last quarter's revenue. A guidance-top-end cut plus capacity delays plus two large target cuts is a genuine thesis impairment, and it is compounding with the factor unwind rather than being rescued by it.
gappers.impact: The least likely name here to mean-revert, and the only one whose drawdown rests on company-specific bad news rather than beta. NBIS has round-tripped from roughly $141 to $108.63, a ~23% drawdown in days, and it is the epicenter of the factor — so it is also the name most exposed to a bad NVDA print on Tuesday. It did bounce with the cohort (-6.26% -> -5.57%), but off the deepest base.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: The capex-financing concern is structural but structurally BEARISH — a long here is catching a falling knife on a real guidance cut into an unresolved binary, the opposite of the strategy's momentum mandate.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Displaces nothing (0 positions, 0/3 trades, full cash), but it is the hardest mechanical reject on the board: ATR(14) $15.27 = 14.1% of price, so the mandated 10% trailing stop sits at 0.71 ATR — well inside a single average day's range and certain to be stopped out by ordinary noise, with a 2:1 target needing +20% from a stop that cannot hold. Also below its 200-SMA. Cannot clear 2:1 at any stop distance the rules permit. No entry.

headlines: Bullish agreed to acquire transfer agent Equiniti for $4.25B, expanding beyond exchange trading into issuer services, 24/7 trading and stablecoin settlement; close expected January 2027 (Binance Square / The Cryptonomist, 2026-05-05)
Bullish Q3 reports pre-market Wednesday Nov 18 with a double-digit move implied by options; October volume $37.7B vs $48.6B in September, spreads 2.43bps (per the 09:09 ET run)
gappers.catalyst_detail: Bullish's standing bull case is the $4.25B acquisition of transfer agent Equiniti, announced 2026-05-05 and still expected to close January 2027, which would move it from a pure crypto exchange into issuer services and tokenized real-world assets. Nothing advanced that today. What is live is the near term: Q3 lands pre-market Wednesday Nov 18 with a double-digit implied move, and the operating metrics heading into it are deteriorating — October volume of $37.7B against $48.6B in September, with average spreads widening to 2.43bps. The stock remains far below its $37 IPO price and a $118 post-IPO high, with consensus around Hold. It also sits on the same weekend crypto flush that hit BMNR, after bitcoin's sixth consecutive weekly loss and a Sunday low of ~$62,100.
gappers.why: Crypto-correlated equities are the highest-beta expression of risk appetite, so BLSH gapped with the asset class. But the mechanism that matters is what happened next: when the whole gapper cohort caught a bid off the open, BLSH did not. A name that will not participate in its own sector's bounce is being distributed, not accumulated — and the obvious reason is the pre-market print 48 hours out with falling volumes and widening spreads.
gappers.impact: This is the one row where the move does NOT read as a one-day headline spike likely to mean-revert, and the evidence is the absence of a bounce rather than the size of the gap. The prior session's 208k shares is thin, which normally argues for reversion, so the refusal to bounce on thin volume is more telling, not less. Read-through: BMNR shared the crypto flush and recovered out of the scan entirely (-7.62% -> -4.49%), which isolates BLSH's weakness as idiosyncratic rather than crypto-wide.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: The Equiniti/tokenization thesis is structural but closes in January 2027, far outside this strategy's swing horizon; everything actionable here is a two-day binary, and the relative weakness argues the market is positioning against the print, not for it.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Displaces nothing (0 positions, 0/3 trades, full cash), and this is exactly the trap the 09:09 ET run flagged: BLSH has one of the better R:R shapes on the board (ATR(14) $1.81 = 8.6% of price, so a 10% stop is 1.17 ATR — the second-tightest-but-least-absurd on the list) precisely BECAUSE it has earnings inside the window. Taking it would be paying for an event, not harvesting an edge. A 2:1 target still needs +20% (2.33 ATR) from a stop inside one day's range, it is below its 20-SMA, and no long should be opened in front of a pre-market print with a double-digit implied move. No entry — and if anything this is a name to keep OFF the buy list through Wednesday.

gappers.catalyst_detail: Bloom Energy's Q3 2026, reported 2026-10-22, was a clean beat: revenue $1,235.8M, up 138.1% from $519.0M, on record product sales, with FY2026 guidance raised to $4.4-4.6B and a 900MW NTT DATA agreement behind it — the on-site data-center power thesis working as advertised. Barclays upgraded to Overweight on 2026-11-03 while cutting its target from $316 to $289, which captures the setup exactly: the business is fine, the multiple is not. Today's gap has no company news behind it, and the stock has now given back the entire +13% post-earnings spike.
gappers.why: BE is a second-derivative AI trade — it sells power to data centers, so it was bid as an AI-capex beneficiary and unwinds as one. When the market questions whether the buildout gets financed (post-Huang, pre-NVDA print), the picks-and-shovels suppliers de-rate alongside the compute providers even though their order books have not changed.
gappers.impact: Orderly institutional mark-down rather than panic, and it bounced with the cohort (-5.92% -> -5.10%), so the one-day-spike reading holds: the fundamentals are intact and the move is multiple compression. Read-through is explicit on this very board — BE, NBIS and CRWV trading as one factor. But a durable bottom most likely requires NVDA's Tuesday print to clear, so a long today is a bet on the event, not on the chart.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: Revenue +138% and raised guidance are structural positives, but today's move is multiple compression into an unresolved binary, and the sector-rotation table does not favor adding AI-adjacent power exposure while the factor is in drawdown.
